subset.rationale: Whole namespace; trivial POD fixture to prove the pipeline.
Self-referential data structure (Node holds std::vector<Node>). Coverage for recursive types + vector-of-self member binding. NOT a BINDER-0004 regression (builds pre-fix too).
Whole namespace; abstract Shape + concrete Circle to prove codegen trampolines and Python-overrides-C++-virtual dispatch.

absl::btree_map/btree_set bound HEAD-ON (the ordered half of BINDER-0008). The container_internal btree_map_container/btree_set_container/btree_container ancestry becomes the flattened/Python-base chain via reachability discovery; the heterogeneous query surface (contains/count/find/erase/at/equal_range/lower_bound/upper_bound and operator[] -> __getitem__ with C++ default-insert semantics) binds via default-instantiable member templates with the TC-0004 dispatch-level substitution. bttest supplies value-setting population (insert's pair<iterator,bool> return is not Python-expressible).
skipped_features: ordered ITERATION from Python (begin/lower_bound return iterator types; a future __iter__/make_iterator feature -- order is exercised natively in the oracle only)
insert/extract/merge from Python (iterator/node_handle returns)
emplace/try_emplace/insert_or_assign (parameter-pack member templates, skipped by design)

subset.rationale: absl::TimeZone (concrete copyable value type: name(), At(Time) -> CivilInfo, ==) and the civil-time types bound head-on. CivilDay/CivilSecond/CivilYear are aliases of time_internal::cctz::detail::civil_time<tag> SPECIALIZATIONS -- real internal-namespace specs bound under their spec-derived Python names (accepted per the reachability-only decision; a friendly-naming pass is future work). Their field accessors (year/month/day/hour/minute/second) and member += (__iadd__, incl. the famous normalization behavior) bind directly. TimeZone::CivilInfo is a NESTED class listed explicitly (nested non-template classes are not auto-discovered); its cs/subsecond/offset/is_dst/zone_abbr members bind (zone_abbr exercises a const char* def_ro). The tztest fixture wraps the free conversion API (UTCTimeZone/FixedTimeZone/LoadTimeZone -> optional, FromCivil/ToCivilSecond/ToCivilDay, FromUnixSeconds/ToUnixSeconds, FormatTime, GetWeekday -> int). Differentials use UTC/fixed-offset zones only (tzdata-independent).
skipped_features: civil-time comparison/difference operators (free function TEMPLATES over <tag>, skipped by design; differential uses field accessors)
TimeZone::At(CivilSecond) -> TimeInfo and NextTransition/PrevTransition (nested TimeInfo/CivilTransition + out-params; not exercised)
named-zone loads in differentials (LoadTimeZone is exposed but tests stick to UTC/fixed offsets for tzdata independence)
ctor default-argument values (C++26 gap: civil ctors bind with all six fields required)

subset.rationale: Binds two specializations of absl::InlinedVector (a small-buffer-optimized vector) DIRECTLY (no wrappers): <int,4> and <double,2> -> distinct Python types InlinedVectorInt4/InlinedVectorDouble2, with the full push_back/pop_back/at/operator[]/front/back/size/capacity/clear/empty/reserve/resize/erase/insert surface; differentially checked vs native Abseil incl. the small-buffer spill -> heap capacity growth. Links the prebuilt absl static lib (InlinedVector::at() -> ThrowStdOutOfRange). The hash/btree containers (flat_hash_map/set, btree_*) and FixedArray are DEFERRED to BINDER-0008: their public query/insert APIs are member templates (heterogeneous lookup) the binder skips, they transitively expose ~35 container_internal types under mangled names, and FixedArray hits an Abseil-internal AsValueType instantiation; a clean binding needs internal-namespace skipping + member-template handling.
skipped_features: flat_hash_map/flat_hash_set/btree_map/btree_set: bind+link OK but explode into container_internal types and their query APIs are member-template-only (BINDER-0008)
absl::FixedArray: Abseil-internal AsValueType<int> instantiation is ill-formed under the toolchain even after the array-member skip (BINDER-0008)

subset.rationale: absl::crc32c_t is a trivial strongly-typed value class bound head-on: default/explicit-uint32 constructors, explicit operator uint32_t -> __int__ (the value channel), and the namespace-scope operator<< -> __str__ ('%08x' hex). The computation/arithmetic API (ComputeCrc32c/ExtendCrc32c/ExtendCrc32cByZeroes/ConcatCrc32c/RemoveCrc32cPrefix/RemoveCrc32cSuffix) is free functions in ^^absl, so a crctest fixture namespace thin-wraps them (reflecting all of ^^absl is not tractable); four of them resolve to compiled code in libabsl_merged.a. Differential: CRC values, extend == compute-of-concat, concat/remove identities vs the native oracle.
skipped_features: MemcpyCrc32c (void* buffer API has no clean Python mapping)
operator==/!= are hidden friends (not enumerable namespace members); equality is exercised via the fixture eq() and the __int__ channel
AbslStringify friend template (member template, skipped by design)

subset.rationale: The BINDER-0008 payoff: absl::flat_hash_map/flat_hash_set/node_hash_map bound HEAD-ON. Reachability discovery (binder Change 1) keeps the container_internal policy explosion out (no FlatHashMapPolicy/Hash/Eq/Alloc types; only signature-reachable internals like node_handle and the raw_hash_map/raw_hash_set ancestry, which becomes the Python base chain). Default-instantiable member templates (binder Change 2 + the TC-0004 dispatch-level substitution workaround) bind the heterogeneous query surface directly: contains/count/find/erase/at/equal_range and operator[] -> __getitem__ (C++ semantics: default-inserts on miss). size/empty/clear/capacity/bucket_count/load_factor/rehash/reserve bind as plain methods. The hmtest fixture supplies only VALUE-SETTING population (put/add): insert()'s pair<iterator,bool> return has no Python representation (iterators are C++-only), and __getitem__ cannot express assignment.
skipped_features: insert/extract from Python (returns pair<iterator,bool>/node_handle; iterator types have no Python value semantics -- population via hmtest::put/add or d[k] default-insert)
emplace/try_emplace/insert_or_assign/lazy_emplace (parameter-pack member templates, skipped by design)
begin/end iteration (iterator-returning; a future __iter__/make_iterator feature)
btree containers (sibling run abseil_btree)
FixedArray (still blocked -- internal AsValueType instantiation; see BINDER-0008)

subset.rationale: absl::int128 / absl::uint128 are concrete 128-bit integer value types — an ideal real-library dunder-mapping target. The binder maps their member + free arithmetic/bitwise/comparison operators to Python dunders (__add__/__sub__/__mul__/__truediv__/__mod__/__and__/__or__/__xor__/__lshift__/__rshift__ + in-place, __eq__/__lt__/...), constructors from built-in integers, and __bool__/__int__/__float__ conversions. Their free operator<<(std::ostream&, ...) is surfaced as Python str() via __str__ (BINDER-0007 fix), used here as the differential oracle's value channel (128-bit results exceed Python-constructible range). Differentially checked vs native Abseil.
skipped_features: int128 has several integral conversion operators that all map to __int__ (last-one-wins picks a narrow one); value read-back in tests uses str(), not int() (see findings/BINDER-0008)
constructing 128-bit values beyond the unsigned-long-long range from Python (no bigint->int128 caster); arithmetic still produces full-width results

subset.rationale: absl::Status is Abseil's canonical error type — a concrete class bound head-on: ok()/code()/raw_code()/message()/ToString()/Update(), constructed from (StatusCode, string_view). absl::StatusCode is a real scoped enum (kOk/kNotFound/kInvalidArgument/...) bound with all values. Exercises the std::string_view and std::optional casters (message() -> string_view; GetPayload -> optional<Cord>). Differentially checked vs native Abseil on code/message/ToString.
skipped_features: payload API (SetPayload/GetPayload/ErasePayload over absl::Cord) not exercised in tests — bound but Cord round-tripping is out of scope for this run
message() returns absl::string_view (= std::string_view here); requires <nanobind/stl/string_view.h>

subset.rationale: absl::Cord -- Abseil's flagship rope/string data structure, a large concrete class -- bound head-on: explicit Cord(string_view) ctor, Append/Prepend (the const Cord&/string_view overloads; the string-like T&& overloads are member templates, skipped by design), RemovePrefix/RemoveSuffix, Subcord, size/empty/Clear, Compare/StartsWith/EndsWith, TryFlat -> optional<string_view>, Flatten, operator<< -> __str__. The classic string FREE-function API is variadic/range templates (StrCat's AlphaNum pack, StrJoin, StrSplit) so the strtest fixture exposes concrete-arity wrappers (cat2/cat3/cat_int/join/split/to_int/upper/lower) -- exercising the string, string_view, vector<string>, and optional casters. absl::string_view == std::string_view here (alias).
skipped_features: string-like Append/Prepend(T&&) overloads (member templates, skipped by design)
CordBuffer paths (Append(CordBuffer)/GetAppendBuffer; move-only buffer type out of scope)
Chunks()/Chars() iteration ranges (nested non-template classes are not auto-discovered; not exercised)
hidden-friend operator==/!= (not enumerable namespace members; Compare()==0 is the equality channel)
SetExpectedChecksum/ExpectedChecksum (optional<uint32> niche)

subset.rationale: absl::Duration and absl::Time are concrete value types bound DIRECTLY: their arithmetic/comparison operators map to Python dunders and operator<<(std::ostream&,...) is surfaced as __str__ (e.g. str(Seconds(90)) == '1m30s'). They have no public integer constructors, so a timetest fixture namespace supplies the real factory/conversion free functions (absl::Seconds/Minutes/Hours/Milliseconds, ToInt64Seconds/..., FromUnixSeconds/ToUnixSeconds) to construct/extract values from Python. Differentially checked vs native Abseil. Exercises the cctz link closure (CoreFoundation).
skipped_features: absl::CivilDay/CivilSecond/... (civil_time<tag> specializations bind under mangled underlying-spec names; deferred for a clean-naming pass)
Duration/Time factory + conversion functions are exercised via timetest wrappers (absl::Seconds etc. are overloaded free functions, not directly namable as a single reflected entity)

subset.rationale: CLI::App is bound head-on through its string-collecting option API -- the path that needs no typed C++ variable, so it crosses to Python with no fixture: add_option(name)/add_flag(name) return an Option whose parsed values stay as strings (results() == list[str]); parse(list[str]) drives a parse from a reversed forward command line (CLI11's parse(vector<string>&) expects the reversed vector, avoiding argc/argv). CLI::Option exposes count/empty/results/get_single_name/get_snames/get_lnames and the configuration chain (required/expected/take_all). The CLI::ParseError hierarchy (RequiredError/ExtrasError/ArgumentMismatch/ConversionError) is reflected so the failure-path differential can compare real CLI exceptions. oracle_native.cpp drives four scenarios (basic option+repeated-flag parse, a 3-value option, a required-missing RequiredError, an unexpected-extra ExtrasError) and the Python test mirrors them exactly. NOTE: the run does NOT reach a clean pass -- the binder defaults raw-pointer-returning methods (add_option/add_flag -> Option*, every fluent setter -> App*/Option*) to rv_policy::automatic (= take_ownership for pointers), but App owns each Option through std::unique_ptr, so Python's wrapper double-frees it. The first parse aborts (SIGABRT) or segfaults inside CLI::App::_process_requirements (when a discarded add_flag return is GC'd early). This is a real binder ownership-default bug, minimized in findings_draft/reflect-raw-ptr-return-take-ownership-default.md; the tests are written against correct behavior and pass once pointer returns default to a non-owning policy. No fixture is used: wrapping add_* in a C++ factory would only hide the bug.
skipped_features: ensure_utf8(char**) and the argv-style parse(int, char**) / parse(int, wchar_t**) overloads: a pointer-to-pointer parameter has no nanobind caster and the binder does not gracefully skip it (it synthesizes a non-matching forwarding lambda -> hard compile error); excluded by member reflection via cli_excluded_marker(). The bindable parse(vector<string>&) is what the run drives. (see findings_draft/binder-ptr-to-ptr-param-no-graceful-skip.md)

typed option binding (add_option(name, T& variable) / add_flag(name, T& variable)): templated on the bound C++ variable's type -- a consteval/template front that cannot reference a Python value, so not bindable; the string-collecting Option.results() path is the bindable equivalent and is what the differential checks
Validator / Formatter / Config subobjects, callbacks (std::function setters), subcommand trees beyond add_subcommand presence: deep auxiliary surface, out of the parse-correctness focus

subset.rationale: moodycamel::ConcurrentQueue<T> is the library's central class, bound head-on for two element types (int, std::string) as explicit specs in the reflect_ pack. Its non-template producer/observer surface binds directly: the two value-capacity constructors (ConcurrentQueue(size_t capacity) and ConcurrentQueue(minCapacity, maxExplicitProducers, maxImplicitProducers)), enqueue(T const&)/enqueue(T&&) and try_enqueue(T const&)/try_enqueue(T&&) (the producer theme), size_approx() (the size theme), and the static is_lock_free(). The dequeue side -- try_dequeue(U& item) -- is a MEMBER TEMPLATE (binder skips member templates) whose result comes back through an OUT-PARAMETER reference with no Python representation; the cqtest namespace supplies the ONLY fixture, a thin optional<T>-returning adapter over the real queue's try_dequeue (the dequeue-from-empty-returns-nullopt path and every dequeued value still come from the real bound queue). The differential drives a single-threaded enqueue/dequeue sequence through both the bound module and the native oracle and compares: FIFO ordering of dequeued ints from a single (implicit) producer, the dequeued value sequence, size_approx() after enqueues and after partial drain, try_enqueue success, dequeue-from-empty returning nullopt, and is_lock_free().
skipped_features: ConcurrentQueue's seven static const config constants (BLOCK_SIZE, MAX_SUBQUEUE_SIZE, EXPLICIT_INITIAL_INDEX_SIZE, IMPLICIT_INITIAL_INDEX_SIZE, INITIAL_IMPLICIT_PRODUCER_HASH_SIZE, EXPLICIT_BLOCK_EMPTY_COUNTER_THRESHOLD, EXPLICIT_CONSUMER_CONSUMPTION_QUOTA_BEFORE_ROTATE) -- in-class-initialized static const with no out-of-line definition; the binder binds static data members BY ADDRESS, which ODR-uses them -> undefined symbol at link. Excluded via a programmatic nb::exclude_ marker (cq_excluded_marker() in binding.cpp). Suspected binder bug, see findings_draft/binder-static-const-member-address-odr-use.md
try_dequeue(U& item) bound head-on -- member template + out-parameter reference; re-expressed as cqtest.try_dequeue_int/_str returning optional<T> (the real queue's try_dequeue still does the work)

ProducerToken / ConsumerToken -- their only constructors are templates taking ConcurrentQueue<T,Traits>& (member/constructor templates, BINDER-0001), so no bindable ctor exists; the token-based enqueue/dequeue overloads are consequently dropped (the token-less overloads cover the single-producer differential)
enqueue_bulk / try_enqueue_bulk / try_dequeue_bulk -- iterator-template fronts (It itemFirst, size_t count); no Python representation of a raw iterator pair
try_dequeue_from_producer / try_dequeue_bulk_from_producer -- require a producer_token_t (unconstructable, see above)
swap (free function + member swap_internal) and the move constructor -- move-only/by-ref-self plumbing, not part of the producer/consumer differential
BlockingConcurrentQueue -- its wait_dequeue blocks a thread; single-threaded differential uses the non-blocking ConcurrentQueue (blocking header still compiles in the Gate-1 probe)

subset.rationale: date's calendrical VALUE types bound head-on: year/month/day (each an opaque integral wrapper with explicit ctor, ok(), and a full free-operator surface), year_month and month_day (the two-field composites), year_month_day (the central y/m/d triple, with its operator sys_days() conversion exercised through the fixture), and weekday. The differential checks calendrical arithmetic (operator+/- with days/months/years free operators -> dunders), the six comparison operators -> rich-comparison dunders, weekday computation from a date, and formatted output. The datefix fixture bridges only what the real API cannot express to Python: the sys_days serial-day round-trip (date::sys_days is std::chrono::time_point<system_clock, days> -- a typedef over a chrono time_point with no nanobind caster, so year_month_day<->sys_days and weekday(sys_days) go through free functions over a plain day-count int) and date::format() (a function TEMPLATE over CharT/Traits/Streamable, unbindable; wrapped to take/return std::string).
skipped_features: tz.h / time-zone database (needs tz.cpp compiled + an IANA tzdata install -- out of scope for the header-only run; only <date/date.h> is bound)

the indexed/last calendar types (weekday_indexed, weekday_last, month_day_last, year_month_day_last, month_weekday[_last], year_month_weekday[_last]) -- secondary surface, the run pins the core value types and their operators
operator++/-- (pre/post increment) -- the binder skips ++/-- per docs (no Python analog)
date::format()/operator<< as bound entities -- function templates over CharT/Traits/Streamable, not bindable; formatted output is exercised through the datefix format_*() std::string wrappers

the chrono duration typedefs days/months/years and sys_days/local_days as bound types -- chrono time_points/durations have no nanobind caster; arithmetic that needs them is reached through the value-type operators (day +/- days etc. take a bound operand) or the datefix serial-day bridge

subset.rationale: Vector3d/Matrix3d -- Eigen::Matrix<double,3,1> and <double,3,3>, the library's flagship concrete types -- bound HEAD-ON. This is the run the nb::exclude_ feature was built for: Eigen's facade methods return expression templates whose own facades mint ever-deeper specializations (transpose() -> Transpose<Derived> -> Transpose<Transpose<...>>; asPermutation() grows Matrix<N> to Matrix<N*N>), so unrestricted discovery DIVERGES, and walking some minted specs (NestByValue<expr>, SparseView under Eigen/Dense) is a hard error. With the expression/view/solver templates and Eigen::internal excluded, discovery converges to exactly 32 specs: the two seeds, Matrix<complex<double>,1,1>/<3,1> (from eigenvalues() declarations), and each one's CRTP facade chain (MatrixBase/DenseBase/PlainObjectBase/DenseCoeffsBase x3/EigenBase) -- which bind as REAL Python bases (the Tier-3 inheritance theme at Tier-5 scale: Matrix -> PlainObjectBase -> MatrixBase -> DenseBase -> DenseCoeffsBase<3/1/0> -> EigenBase, all isinstance-checkable). The bound member surface is the non-template facade API (norm/squaredNorm/sum/prod/mean/trace/determinant/coeff access via __call__ and __getitem__/setZero/setOnes/normalize/normalized/rows/cols/size, Vector3d's real (x,y,z) ctor, *=/ /= -> __imul__/__idiv__, streamability -> __str__). Eigen's arithmetic operators are function templates returning expression types -- intrinsically outside the binder's model (member templates bind only via all-defaulted default instantiation) -- so the eigentest fixture supplies the eager-value arithmetic (add/scale/dot/cross/matmul/matvec/transpose/inverse/solve/symmetric-eigenvalues), all taking/returning the BOUND Matrix types by value, exercising the registered-type caster path differentially.
skipped_features: expression-template returns (transpose/inverse/diagonal/block/head/tail/cwise*/replicate/reverse/asDiagonal/asPermutation/homogeneous/colwise/rowwise/real/imag/...) -- excluded via nb::exclude_; the eager-value equivalents are exercised through the eigentest fixture
solver/decomposition objects (LLT/LDLT/*LU/*QR/SVD/eigensolvers/Jacobi) -- excluded; solve exercised eagerly via the fixture's partialPivLu().solve()
Map/Ref views (raw-pointer semantics have no Python value story)

fixed-size convenience ctors on WRONG-sized specs (Matrix(x,y,z) is a plain member of EVERY Matrix with a size static_assert in its BODY -- lazily ill-formed, undetectable by reflection; excluded per-member by reflection, the exclude_ member-level escape hatch). Same mechanism for the handful of facade members whose bodies are lazily ill-formed for some bound spec (e.g. eulerAngles on a vector).
comma-initializer (operator<<(Scalar) -> CommaInitializer, excluded -- a C++ syntactic device with no Python equivalent)
templated arithmetic operators (return expression types; see rationale)

subset.rationale: tl::expected<T,E> is the library's whole point, bound head-on as three real specializations (int/std::string value-or-error, the role-swapped std::string/int, and the no-value success channel void/std::string): default + copy ctors, has_value(), explicit operator bool -> __bool__, the all-defaulted member templates value<U=T>() (real throw path -> bad_expected_access) and swap<OT,OE>(), and the non-template error() overload set. tl::unexpected<std::string>/<int> are listed for their REAL non-template ctors (a Python str/int constructs one directly) + value(); tl::bad_expected_access<std::string> for ctor/error()/what() (its thrown form surfaces in Python as RuntimeError('Bad expected access'), differentially checked). The extest fixture supplies factories (every value/error converting ctor is a template, skipped by design) plus thin wrappers over the all-template fronts: the free operator== family, value_or<U>, and map/and_then with fixed C++ callables. FORMERLY OUTCOME B behind a five-bug cascade, all fixed -- the run is green end-to-end: TC-0008 (mangler ICE on tl's namespace-scope deduction guide in the binder's namespace walks; the toolchain mangles guide reflections now AND the binder strips guides pre-lift), BINDER-0012 (`unexpected() = delete;` bound as init<>; deleted functions filtered on every path now), TC-0006/TC-0007 (the void spec wrong-rejected by eager member-body instantiation and SEGV'd by can_substitute on swap<OT=void>; it now binds, with value/swap gracefully not-substitutable-for-void), TC-0009 (the four same-headed value() overload templates of a specialization mangled identically as reflection NTTPs -- ODRHash::AddFunctionDecl no-ops in specialization context -- so codegen folded the binder's dispatch bodies and value() silently never bound; found by THIS run's first post-fix execution), and BINDER-0013 (copy ctors were never bound; init<const T&> now binds for copyable non-trampolined classes).
skipped_features: all value/error converting constructors + in_place/unexpect tag ctors (templates, skipped by design; extest factories instead)

monadic and_then/map/transform/or_else and value_or (member templates with a non-defaulted F/U parameter -- not default-instantiable; extest wraps map/and_then/value_or with fixed callables as the differential channel)
emplace (parameter-pack member template, skipped by design)
free operator==/!= family and free swap/make_unexpected (free function templates -- not bindable; extest eq_* wrappers cover equality)
operator*/operator-> accessors (unary deref has no Python dunder; value() is the access path)
&&/const&&-qualified value()/error()/unexpected::value() overloads (binder qualifier matrix skips rvalue-ref-qualified)

expected<void, E>'s value<U=T>() and swap<OT=T,...>() (enable_if'd away for T=void: can_substitute reports not-substitutable -- TC-0006's graceful path -- and the binder skips them; has_value/__bool__/error/ctors are the void surface)

subset.rationale: fast_float's API front is free function templates `from_chars(UC const* first, UC const* last, T& value, fmt/base)` returning `from_chars_result_t<UC>` -- pointer pairs and an out-param reference, none of which Python can express, so the `fixture` namespace wraps the four concrete instantiations (double/float/int64/uint64) as string-in -> {value, consumed, ok, ec}-out (a from_chars_advanced variant carries a parse_options_t for custom decimal point). But the library's OWN bindable value types are reflected head-on, not wrapped: (1) `fast_float::chars_format`, the bitset format enum, all ten named members (scientific/fixed/hex/no_infnan/general/json/json_or_infnan/fortran/allow_leading_plus/skip_white_space) bound and their underlying uint64 values differentially checked against the native oracle; (2) `parse_options_t<char>`, the options struct, ctor `(fmt, dot:str, base:int)` + its three mutable fields (decimal_point is a C++ `char` surfaced as a 1-char str) -- driven through parse_double_opts to prove the custom decimal point actually changes parsing; (3) `from_chars_result_t<char>`, the {ptr, ec} result + its P2497 `operator bool`. The Layer-1 differential locks in parsed values across the hard cases (smallest subnormal 5e-324, an exact round-to-even tie 1.0000000000000002, overflow->inf with errc=ERANGE, inf/nan literals, single-precision rounding), chars consumed (trailing junk, empty, error), ok flags + raw errc codes, format gating (scientific rejects fixed and vice versa; hex mode does not consume an 0x prefix), and integer/unsigned parsing across bases incl. uint64 max + overflow.
skipped_features: from_chars / from_chars_advanced bound directly -- free function templates over (UC const* first, UC const* last, T& value): a C-pointer pair plus an out-parameter reference, neither Python-expressible. Wrapped per-instantiation by the fixture namespace (string in -> {value, consumed, ok, ec}); the wrappers are the only way to reach the parser from Python.

C++ default argument VALUES on the wrappers (parse_double's fmt, parse_int's base): a standard C++26 reflection gap -- the binder cannot recover default-arg values, so fmt/base must be passed explicitly from Python (matches the spdlog run's note).

chars_format bitwise combination from Python (the free operator| / operator& / operator~ over the enum): reflecting the enum alone does not pull the free operators in, and the binder emits an ordinary (non-flag) enum, so `general | allow_leading_plus` is not expressible. The pre-combined named members (general, json, json_or_infnan, fortran) cover the common cases differentially.

from_chars_result_t<char>.ec field: the getter returns std::errc, for which nanobind has no type caster, so reading `.ec` raises TypeError (the binder bound the field head-on; the caster gap is the limitation). ptr (const char*) and operator bool ARE observable; the fixture wrappers surface the errc as a plain int instead. See findings_draft.
integer_times_pow10 free functions (uint64/int64 mantissa * 10^exp -> double): a numeric utility orthogonal to the from_chars parsing theme this run pins; not bound.
the std::float16_t/bfloat16_t/float32_t/float64_t from_chars instantiations: extended-float types whose Python representation is just double; double+float cover the rounding behavior differentially.

subset.rationale: Four layers of REAL fmt surface, all differentially checked vs native fmt. (1) fmt's enums color (~140 CSS-color enumerators)/terminal_color/emphasis, reflected directly. (2) fmt's real concrete class fmt::format_int (its fast int->string formatter): ctor overloads + str()/c_str()/data()/size() bind, private member templates skipped. (3) fmt's real FORMATTING API bound DIRECTLY from its own function-template instantiations fmt::to_string<int/double/long long> (the binder binds fmt's own symbol, not a wrapper). fmt's format()/print() front-ends take a CONSTEVAL format_string<Args...> first parameter not constructible at runtime from Python, so they are intrinsically not directly bindable; to_string<T>/format_int are the directly-bindable formatting entry points. (4) A fixture namespace fmttest of concrete wrappers over the runtime fmt::format engine that drives the remaining Tier-2 themes: keyword arguments (P3096 names -> nb::arg), std::string/std::vector casters incl. fmt::join, and the member-function-template gap (Formatter::apply<T> skipped while ordinary members bind).
skipped_features: fmt::format/format_to/print/println front-ends: intrinsically not directly bindable (consteval format_string<Args...> first param); runtime path exercised via fmttest wrappers
fmt::format_int private member templates format_signed/format_unsigned (binder skips member templates)
Formatter::apply<T> member function template (binder gracefully skips member templates)

subset.rationale: glm is entirely templates; bind concrete vec3/vec4. Components live in an anonymous union (not exposed, BINDER-0002); usable surface is constructors, operator[]->__getitem__, static length(). Free-function API is function templates (not auto-bound).
skipped_features: anonymous-union components x/y/z/w (BINDER-0002)
free-function templates (length/dot/cross/normalize)
mat types
operators (free function templates)

subset.rationale: cpp-httplib's client + value types are bound head-on and driven over real loopback (127.0.0.1, ephemeral port). httplib::Client is the REAL client: its string-path/body/content-type Get/Post/Put/Delete overloads bind, and Python drives them against a real httplib::Server. EVERY Get/Delete overload takes a DownloadProgress (std::function) parameter, so <nanobind/stl/function.h> is included and std::function is bound; the no-callback overloads still need the progress arg passed explicitly (a real always-continue lambda; None is not an empty std::function, and the default nullptr is a C++26-unbindable default VALUE), and the native oracle passes the identical callback so both sides drive the same call. httplib::Request/Response are the value types -- method/path/body/status/reason data members plus the has_header/get_header_value/get_param_value/set_header/set_content accessor methods (headers are round-tripped through these string accessors since Headers is an unordered_multimap with no caster). httplib::Result is the Get/Post return type: error()->Error, value()/operator*->Response&, operator bool, request-header accessors. httplib::Error + httplib::StatusCode are the enums, differentially checked. The httptest::EchoServer fixture owns ONLY what httplib forces into C++: a background-thread accept loop (bind_to_any_port + listen_after_bind + wait_until_ready + stop) and std::function echo handlers registered in C++ that reflect request method/path/body/headers back into the response. The differential: the native oracle drives the IDENTICAL client calls against the SAME fixture server and emits status codes, response bodies, content types, echoed headers, and the Error enum on a closed-port connect; the Python test drives the bound client the same way and asserts equality.
skipped_features: Server bound only via the fixture (its Get/Post/... handler registration takes std::function Handler values that run on the server thread -- not Python callables; the EchoServer fixture registers them in C++). The thread lifecycle (listen_after_bind on a background std::thread) is likewise not Python-expressible.

std::function-typed handler/provider params other than progress (ContentReceiver/ResponseHandler/ContentProvider overloads expose httplib::DataSink as an opaque param type and run code on the C++ side -- bound but not exercised; the body/content-type + progress overloads are the driven surface)

Headers (unordered_multimap, custom case-insensitive hash/equal) + Params (multimap) parameters/members -- no nanobind multimap caster; the Get/Post overloads taking them skip, and headers/params are exercised through the string get_header_value/set_header/get_param_value accessors
multipart form-data surface (MultipartFormData/UploadFormData/FormDataProvider, the *FormDataItems vectors) -- unbound user types; the multipart Post/Put overloads skip
streaming surface (Result's StreamHandle ctor, open_stream, the ContentReader/DataSink/Stream-based reads, the second free-function Result class) -- unbound internal-impl types; excluded
char-pointer-and-length Post/Put/Patch overloads (const char* body, size_t content_length) -- the std::string-body overloads cover the same behavior bindably

default-argument VALUES (def='' / id=0 on get_header_value etc., status=Found_302 on set_redirect) are a C++26 reflection gap; the tests pass defaulted args explicitly, matching the native oracle's C++ defaults

subset.rationale: nlohmann::json = basic_json<>; the whole real value type is reflected (no facade). Value-ingestion/extraction is all member templates (correctly skipped), so jsontest helper factories supply populated inputs; the binder still exposes the real dump()/is_*()/size()/operator[]/== surface under test. Previously OUTCOME B: reflecting basic_json crashed clang-p2996 — originally mis-attributed to a constexpr/SLoc-exhaustion ceiling (TC-0002), but root-caused to a use-after-free in Sema (fixed in the pinned toolchain). With the fix + a raised constexpr-step budget, the real class binds.
skipped_features: all member templates: get<T>/parse/get_to/emplace_back/compat-ctors (Python uses jsontest factories instead)

subset.rationale: linalg is entirely templates; vec<float,3> is the only concrete auto-bindable surface (data x/y/z, ctors, operator[]). Free-function API is function templates (not auto-bound).
skipped_features: free-function templates (dot/length/normalize/...)
mat<> types

subset.rationale: pugixml's DOM handle objects are bound head-on: xml_document (the DOM root, parsed via load_string) inheriting xml_node publicly (the inheritance theme -- xml_node is in the bind set so it is the real Python base, not flattened), xml_node (the lightweight node handle -- type/name/value/child/attribute/child_value/first_child/last_child/next_sibling/previous_sibling/parent/empty + comparison dunders + the bool/append/set mutators), xml_attribute (the attribute handle -- name/value/as_int/as_uint/as_double/as_bool/empty/next_attribute + comparisons), and xml_parse_result (the parse-status struct -- status/offset/encoding data members + description()). The three enums (xml_node_type, xml_encoding, xml_parse_status) are bound with all values and differentially checked. The pugitest fixture supplies ONLY serialization (to_xml: node.print into an ostringstream -> std::string), which pugixml exposes only through an xml_writer/std::ostream front Python cannot drive. Differential: the native oracle parses a fixed XML document and emits node names, attribute values, child-traversal order, typed attribute conversions, parse status, and the serialized output; the Python test parses the same string through the binding and asserts equality on all of it.
skipped_features: serialization via xml_writer / std::basic_ostream (print/save) -- no ostream caster; surfaced as a string through the pugitest.to_xml fixture instead

iterator/range traversal (begin/end/children/attributes -> xml_node_iterator/xml_attribute_iterator/xml_named_node_iterator/xml_object_range) -- excluded; first_child/next_sibling cover traversal head-on
xml_text accessor (xml_node::text() -> xml_text) -- excluded; child_value() covers text access head-on
xml_tree_walker visitor (xml_node::traverse) -- needs a Python-implemented virtual (two-stage); excluded
the whole XPath surface (select_node/select_nodes -> xpath_node/xpath_node_set, xpath_query, xpath_variable_set) -- unbound user types; excluded

unspecified_bool_type conversion operator -- returns a function-pointer type with no numeric dunder; the binder's reflect_bind_conversion skips it (no __bool__ -- that needs a bool-returning conversion)
find_attribute/find_child/find_node member templates (Predicate non-defaulted) -- skipped per the member-template-needs-explicit-args limitation

internal_object()/the explicit xml_*(xml_*_struct*) ctors -- return/take the forward-declared INCOMPLETE structs xml_node_struct/xml_attribute_struct; binding them instantiated nanobind's caster on an incomplete type (typeid/is_base_of of an incomplete type, a hard compile error), so both structs are in the exclude_ pack and those members are skipped (the structs are an internal implementation detail with no Python meaning)

default-argument VALUES (load_string's options=parse_default, the as_* getters' def, child/attribute's etc.) are a C++26 reflection gap (P3096 exposes has_default_argument but not the value); the tests pass every defaulted arg explicitly, matching the native oracle's C++ defaults so both sides drive identical calls

append_buffer/load_buffer (const void*/void* contents) bound but not exercised; the unspecified_bool_type conversion operator is skipped by reflect_bind_conversion (function-pointer result, no numeric dunder)

subset.rationale: simdjson's DOM value types are bound head-on: dom::element (the JSON node handle -- type() -> element_type, the nine is_*() discriminants is_array/is_object/is_string/is_int64/is_uint64/is_double/is_number/is_bool/is_null/is_bigint, and operator==/operator< over elements), dom::array and dom::object (size()), the element_type enum (ARRAY/OBJECT/INT64/UINT64/DOUBLE/STRING/BOOL/NULL_VALUE/BIGINT, the type-discriminant theme, differentially checked), and the error_code enum (the full parse/navigation taxonomy SUCCESS..NUM_ERROR_CODES). simdjson's entire navigation+coercion surface returns simdjson_result<T> (a value-or-error monad with no Python caster) off a MOVE-ONLY parser whose returned handles alias parser-owned buffers -- neither expressible to Python -- so the simdjsontest fixture supplies ONLY that: Doc owns the parser+padded source and yields the root as a bound dom::element; at_key/at_pointer/at_index/array_at/object_at navigate (unwrapping simdjson_result<element> to the SAME bound element, throwing QueryError carrying the raw error_code on NO_SUCH_FIELD/INDEX_OUT_OF_BOUNDS/INCORRECT_TYPE); as_array/as_object/as_int64/as_uint64/as_double/as_bool/as_string coerce; array_values/object_keys materialize children/keys in document order. Differential: the native oracle parses one fixed JSON document and emits scalar reads (int/uint/double/bool/string), array+object sizes, key lookups, JSON-pointer navigation, type discriminants for every value kind, document-order array elements and object keys, is_null/number coercions, and error codes for malformed JSON + missing keys + wrong-type coercions; the Python test parses the identical string through the binding and asserts equality on all of it plus enum-value and isinstance invariants.
skipped_features: the ondemand API (simdjson::ondemand::*) -- forward-iteration-constrained, single-pass, and template-heavy (value/field/object/array are tied to a live iterator); the random-access DOM API is the bindable + differentiable surface

simdjson_result<T> (every navigation/coercion return) -- a value-or-error monad template with no Python caster; surfaced through the simdjsontest fixture's unwrap helpers (result -> value, throwing QueryError carrying the raw error_code)

dom::parser entry points (parse/load/parse_many/load_many) -- parser is move-only and its results alias parser-owned buffers; the Doc fixture owns the parser+source and exposes the root element (parse_many/load_many additionally return document_stream, a streaming front with no Python meaning)
dom::document -- move-only, std::unique_ptr<uint64_t[]>/<uint8_t[]> members; an internal buffer holder with no standalone Python use (the parser owns one)

element::get<T>()/is<T>() member templates (non-defaulted type param) -- skipped per the member-template-needs-explicit-args limitation; the non-template get_int64()/get_bool()/... are surfaced via the fixture's as_* coercions

iteration via begin()/end() on element/array/object -> dom::array::iterator/object::iterator (forward iterators returning element/key_value_pair; no Python iterator protocol bound) -- array_values/object_keys materialize the children/keys head-on instead
padded_string / padded_string_view (the SIMDJSON_PADDING-aware parse-input types) -- the fixture takes a std::string and pads internally; not separately useful to Python
operator std::string_view / operator int64_t / ... implicit conversions on element (SIMDJSON_EXCEPTIONS path) -- ambiguous as Python dunders; explicit as_* coercions are surfaced instead
at_path/at_path_with_wildcard (JSONPath) and the deprecated at(string_view) overload -- JSONPath returns std::vector<element>/results; at_pointer (RFC 6901) covers pointer navigation head-on

default-argument VALUES (parse's realloc_if_needed, allocate's max_depth, parse_many's batch_size) are a C++26 reflection gap (P3096 exposes has_default_argument, not the value); not exercised -- the fixture's helpers take no defaulted args

subset.rationale: spdlog::logger is the library's central class, bound head-on: ctors (name / name+sink_ptr), the non-template log(level, string_view) overloads, set_level/level/should_log/name/set_pattern/flush/flush_on/flush_level, sinks() -> vector<shared_ptr<sink>> (the shared_ptr theme), and clone() -> shared_ptr<logger>. spdlog::level is the namespace carrying the level_enum plus to_string_view/to_short_c_str/from_str (the log-level-enum theme, differentially checked). sinks::sink is the abstract base and sinks::stdout_sink_mt a real concrete sink; the intermediate stdout_sink_base<console_mutex> is LISTED EXPLICITLY so the whole 3-level chain binds as real Python bases (the inheritance theme) -- its only signature self-mentions are deleted copy/move operators, which pull nothing into the bind set (BINDER-0012), so without the explicit opt-in it would flatten. The logtest fixture owns an ostringstream-backed ostream_sink and hands it out as shared_ptr<sinks::sink>, so Python-driven logging is captured as text and compared byte-for-byte against the native oracle driving the identical sequence. Built with SPDLOG_USE_STD_FORMAT (a first-class spdlog config) so string_view_t/format_string_t are the std types the nanobind casters cover; the default bundled-fmt mode's fmt::basic_string_view has no caster.
skipped_features: templated log front-ends (logger::info/warn/... take std::format_string<Args...> -- consteval first param, intrinsically not bindable; the non-template log(level, string_view) overloads are the bindable surface)
Python-implemented custom sinks (sink's pure virtuals need a two-stage trampoline; virtual-override path already proven by _fixture_virtual, kept out of this run)
set_formatter(unique_ptr<formatter>) -- by-value move-only param, skipped per BINDER-0010
sinks_init_list ctor (initializer_list has no Python representation)
ostream_sink bound directly (ctor takes std::ostream& -- no caster; wrapped by the logtest CaptureSink fixture instead)

subset.rationale: Taskflow's three core classes are bound head-on: tf::Taskflow (the task-graph container -- num_tasks/empty/name/dump()->string/clear), tf::Task (the lightweight task handle -- name/num_successors/num_predecessors/num_strong_dependencies/num_weak_dependencies/empty/has_work/hash_value + == / != dunders), and tf::Executor (the work-stealing scheduler -- num_workers from an explicit worker-count ctor arg, plus num_topologies/num_taskflows/num_observers). The graph-construction front (FlowBuilder::emplace / Task::precede / succeed) is entirely templated over C++ callables and variadic Task packs and cannot be driven from Python, so the tftest.Diamond fixture builds a FIXED diamond graph (A -> {B,C} -> D) whose task bodies append their names to an execution-order log and bump an atomic counter; it hands out the REAL tf::Taskflow + tf::Task handles (queried head-on for shape) and drives a REAL tf::Executor::run().wait() for execution. tftest.Engine owns a tf::Executor constructed with an EXPLICIT worker count and hands out the real tf::Executor (its sole ctor's move-only 2nd param leaves it unconstructable from Python directly). Both fixtures return the real classes by POINTER, not reference: a method returning T& to a registered class currently defaults to rv_policy::copy and aborts on these move-only types (see findings_draft/lvalue-ref-class-return-copy-policy.md); a raw class-pointer return is borrowed correctly. Differential: the native oracle builds the identical diamond through the same fixture, then emits graph-shape numbers (num_tasks; per-task num_successors/num_predecessors/strong/weak for A/B/C/D), the executor worker count from an explicit ctor arg, the post-run task-body count, and order-constraint booleans; the Python test asserts equality on all shape numbers + worker count + counter and the dependency ORDER CONSTRAINTS (A first, D last, B and C both after A and before D) rather than exact interleavings.
skipped_features: FlowBuilder::emplace / Task::precede / succeed -- variadic templates over C++ callables and Task packs; not Python-expressible (the whole graph-construction front). Graph wiring is done in the tftest.Diamond fixture; the resulting REAL Task handles are queried head-on.

tf::Executor::run / corun and the algorithm fronts (for_each/transform/reduce/sort/pipeline) -- all templated over callables; run is driven through the fixture and returns tf::Future<void> (inherits std::future<void>, no caster, excluded).

tf::Executor's SOLE constructor Executor(size_t N, std::unique_ptr<WorkerInterface> = nullptr) -- the move-only/excluded 2nd param means the binder binds NO __init__ for Executor (it imports with 'no constructor defined'), so Python cannot construct one directly. The tftest.Engine fixture constructs it with N workers and hands out the real tf::Executor; num_workers() is checked against the N passed. (Not a bug -- the only ctor genuinely isn't Python-expressible; just noting Executor is fixture-constructed.)

lvalue-reference returns of registered classes (tf::Taskflow& / tf::Executor&) -- the binder defaults T& returns to rv_policy::copy, which aborts at runtime on these move-only types (findings_draft/lvalue-ref-class-return-copy-policy.md). The fixture returns tf::Taskflow*/tf::Executor* (borrowed) instead; no real taskflow method returning T& is bound head-on in this run.

library: taskflow v4.0.0 uses std::bit_ceil/std::bit_width (core/wsq.hpp, core/executor.hpp) but never #includes <bit>; on this from-source libc++ <bit> is not pulled in transitively, so <taskflow/taskflow.hpp> fails to compile. Worked around by #include <bit> before the umbrella header in the fixture/binding (findings_draft/taskflow-missing-bit-include.md -- library-side missing-include).

Taskflow::dump(std::ostream&) / Task::dump(std::ostream&) -- ostream& param, no caster; the no-arg Taskflow::dump()->std::string overload is bound and exercised (DOT output is non-deterministic across hash-ordered traversal so its TEXT is not asserted, only that it is non-empty and mentions every task name).
Task::for_each_successor / for_each_predecessor / for_each_subflow_task -- template visitor params; successor/predecessor COUNTS are checked head-on via num_successors/num_predecessors instead.
tf::Future<void> (Executor::run result), tf::Graph, tf::FlowBuilder, tf::WorkerInterface -- excluded; internal / templated / non-bindable types surfaced through the fixture's run() instead.
default-argument VALUES (Executor's N = hardware_concurrency()) are a C++26 reflection gap; the fixture/tests pass an explicit worker count so both sides drive identical ctors.

subset.rationale: tinyobjloader's parse output is a set of plain-aggregate structs; they are bound head-on via reflection: index_t (vertex/normal/texcoord indices), mesh_t (vector<index_t> indices, num_face_vertices, material_ids, smoothing_group_ids, vector<tag_t> tags), shape_t (name + mesh + path), attrib_t (vector<real_t> vertices/normals/texcoords/colors), and material_t (name, illum, the texname strings, the std::map<string,string> unknown_parameter, and the texture_option_t texopts). tag_t, path_t, texture_option_t and texture_type_t are pulled in transitively as reachable member types and bound too. LoadObj is an out-param front (fills attrib_t*/vector<shape_t>*/vector<material_t>* + string* warn/err from a filename or istream), unreachable from Python; the objtest::parse_obj fixture drives the std::istream* overload over an in-memory .obj string and returns objtest::LoadResult AGGREGATING the library's own real attrib_t/vector<shape_t>/vector<material_t>. The differential parses the SAME .obj through native tinyobj and compares vertex/normal/texcoord counts and values, per-shape names, mesh face indices (vertex_index per index_t), num_face_vertices, material_ids, and material name/illum -- all read off the binder-exposed real types.
skipped_features: material_t / texture_option_t C-array fields (real_t ambient[3], diffuse[3], scale[3], ... and char imfchan): fixed-size C arrays are skipped by the binder (def_rw's setter is ill-formed for array members) -- color triples are not in the differential; the bound scalar/string/map material fields are
LoadObj filename overload and the .mtl MaterialReader/MaterialFileReader/MaterialStreamReader hierarchy (filesystem + virtual operator() -- the in-memory istream path is what the fixture drives)
LoadObjWithCallback / callback_t (function-pointer callback struct -- no Python representation)
ParseTextureNameAndOption / LoadMtl (out-param free functions, same shape as LoadObj; the .obj path is the bound surface)

subset.rationale: toml++'s VALUE-TYPE surface is bound head-on: toml::date (year/month/day; its comparison operators are hidden friends, not reflectable namespace members), toml::time (hour/minute/second/nanosecond), toml::time_offset (minutes), toml::date_time (date/time/offset + is_local()), the toml::node_type discriminant enum (all 10 values), and the parse-error surface toml::parse_error (description/source/what) + toml::source_region (begin/end) + toml::source_position (line/column). These are the library's OWN real types, and the differential reads/round-trips real instances of them (date/time fields, enum values, error line/column). The document-tree classes (toml::node/table/array/value<T> and the exceptions-off parse_result) are NOT bound: every node class declares `virtual bool is_homogeneous(node_type, node*& first_nonmatch) noexcept` and the binder hard-errors on the non-const lvalue-reference-to-pointer out-param instead of skipping it (a binder gap; per-overload nb::exclude_ is ineffective for it -- findings_draft/binder-lvalue-ref-to-pointer-param.md). The tomlfix namespace therefore parses + walks the tree in C++ using the LIBRARY's own parse(), node::value<T>() coercion, and toml_formatter/json_formatter, returning plain Python values plus the bound date/time structs and the real node_type/parse_error objects. The differential parses one TOML document natively and from Python and compares: parse success, table size + top-level keys, node_type of representative keys, coerced scalars (incl. nested dotted-key access and permissive int-of-float -> None), real date/time/date_time field values + is_local()/offset, integer-array contents + mixed-array element types, byte-for-byte TOML and JSON round-trip serialization, and the parse-error path (bad TOML -> failed + description + error line/column on the real parse_error/source_region).
skipped_features: toml::node / table / array / value<T> / parse_result -- NOT BOUND: every node class declares is_homogeneous(node_type, node*& first_nonmatch); the binder hard-errors on the node*& (non-const lvalue-ref-to-pointer) out-param instead of skipping it, and a per-overload nb::exclude_ of exactly those overloads does not suppress the bind. Tree navigation runs in C++ (tomlfix, using the library's parse/coerce/format) and surfaces plain Python values + the bound value structs. See findings_draft/binder-lvalue-ref-to-pointer-param.md.
toml::parse(...) overload set (string_view/u8string_view/std::istream&/wstring_view source paths) -- wrapped by a single tomlfix std::string entry point (the parsing is the library's).

node::value<T>() / value_exact<T>() -- consteval template accessors with an explicit type arg; reached via tomlfix::get_int/float/bool/string/date/time/datetime forwarders (the coercion is the library's).

operator<<(std::ostream&, ...) and the toml_formatter/json_formatter/yaml_formatter objects -- ostream-based, no Python representation; wrapped by tomlfix::to_toml/to_json which run the library's real formatters into a string.

source_region::path + the source_path_ptr-taking parse_error ctors -- std::shared_ptr<const std::string> (excluded; shared_ptr<T> binding needs T to be a bound class, but std::string has a type caster).

table/array mutation (insert/emplace/push_back), node_view operator[] proxies, and the constrained template ctors of date/time/date_time -- template-heavy / proxy / template-ctor fronts; the run is parse/read oriented.

subset.rationale: ankerl::unordered_dense::map<int,std::string> and set<int> bound HEAD-ON: the library's public alias templates resolve to detail::table<...> specializations, listed explicitly in the reflect_ pack. The query/mutation surface binds directly off the spec -- the non-template at(Key const&)/operator[](Key const&)->__getitem__ (C++ semantics: default-inserts on miss)/erase(Key const&)->size_t, plus the heterogeneous (member-template) contains/count/find, and size/empty/clear/bucket_count/load_factor/max_load_factor as plain methods. Differential drives the identical lookup/erase/grow scenario through the native oracle and compares sizes, lookup results, default-insert semantics, and erase return codes.

begin/end/find iteration (iterator-returning; a future __iter__/make_iterator feature -- find binds but its iterator return is not value-compared)
segmented_map/segmented_set + PMR variants (same table template, IsSegmented/allocator differ; the standard map/set are the representative head-on bind)
extract/replace/values()/reserve/rehash (value_container_type / node-handle returns with no Python value semantics)
constructors taking bucket_count/Hash/KeyEqual/allocator (defaulted/initializer_list/iterator-range forms have no Python representation; default-construct + populate is the bound path)
